title: Four Manchester Universities Offer £10,000 GREAT Scholarships to Indian Students
excerpt: Manchester Metropolitan, the University of Manchester, Salford and the Royal Northern College of Music join GREAT Scholarships 2027 for Indian postgraduates starting in autumn 2027.
body:
• Four Greater Manchester universities have joined GREAT Scholarships 2027, offering Indian students a minimum of £10,000 towards tuition for a one-year postgraduate course.
  • The four are Manchester Metropolitan University, the Royal Northern College of Music, the University of Manchester and the University of Salford, for entry in autumn 2027 (2027-28).
  • Reader action: you must first hold an offer from a participating university and meet its entry requirements — apply for the course before the scholarship.
  • Subjects span Finance, Marketing, Business, Psychology, STEM, Design and Humanities, plus Arts, Music and Dance.

Four universities in Greater Manchester will offer GREAT Scholarships to Indian students starting postgraduate study in autumn 2027, the British Council announced on Wednesday. Each scholarship is worth a minimum of £10,000 towards tuition fees for a one-year postgraduate taught course in the 2027-28 academic year.

The participating institutions are Manchester Metropolitan University, the Royal Northern College of Music, the University of Manchester and the University of Salford. The announcement, supported by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, was made during the Northern England India Mission's visit to India, as reported in the original India Today coverage.

How the scholarship works

GREAT Scholarships are jointly funded by the UK government's GREAT Britain Campaign, the British Council and participating universities, and run as part of the Study UK programme. The mechanism matters: this is not a standalone cash award you apply for in isolation. Students intending to apply must first have received an offer of entry from one of the participating universities and must satisfy all entry requirements for their chosen course, as specified by that university.

The range is deliberately broad. Alongside business-school staples such as Finance, Marketing and Business, the scholarships cover Psychology, STEM subjects, Design and Humanities, and — reflecting the Royal Northern College of Music's inclusion — Arts, Music and Dance programmes.

"The inclusion of four Greater Manchester universities in the GREAT Scholarships 2027 programme adds further depth to these opportunities."

— Rittika Chanda Parruck MBE, Director Education India, British Council

Why Greater Manchester is pitching to India

Senior representatives from all four universities travelled with the Northern England delegation, which is seeking long-term partnerships with India and deeper links between institutions. The pitch to students goes beyond the £10,000: the British Council pointed to the region's academic, cultural and industry ecosystem, and to post-study work routes that let graduates gain professional experience after their course.

Jo Purves, Pro-Vice Chancellor for Partnerships and Global Engagement at the University of Salford, said the university looked forward to supporting Indian students as they develop their skills and make the most of studying in Greater Manchester.

What applicants should do now

For Indian students targeting autumn 2027, the sequence is clear: choose a one-year postgraduate taught course at one of the four universities, secure an offer, and then apply for the GREAT Scholarship through that university, meeting its stated entry requirements. Because the award is a minimum of £10,000 against tuition only, families should still budget for the remaining fees and living costs in Manchester.

The expansion also lands in a competitive market for Indian postgraduates, where scholarship value, post-study work options and industry links increasingly decide between otherwise similar offers. Four institutions in one city region joining the same programme gives applicants an unusual chance to compare courses — and total costs — within a single, well-connected metro.
